audit.why: Hwei owns the pre-item poke war; Mel flips it at first item and out-scales. Content, packet chart and prose agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides were blanket 'Skill' with all whys describing Mel winning, contradicting content win[] and the packet chart (Hwei rows 0-4, Mel rows 5-6).
audit.why: His layered palette poke out-ranges Radiant Volley until Mel's first-item spike.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-4 flipped to Hwei with rewritten whys; rows 5-6 to Mel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fabricated ability name 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' across the full layer — real E is Subject: Torment. Content misassigns subspells: 'QQ (Severing Bolt)' (Severing Bolt is QW), 'QE (Grim Visage)' (Grim Visage is EQ), 'EE (Stirring Sands)' (no such spell — WE is Stirring Lights, escape is WQ Fleeting Current), 'EQ (Fleeting Current) knock-up' (Fleeting Current is WQ and no knock-up; the fight-deciding E-palette CC is EW Gaze of the Abyss). Also missing: his W palette's shield absorbs your burst.
audit.why: Kit lists palette subspells in Q/W/E order: Q = Devastating Fire/Severing Bolt/Molten Fissure, W = Fleeting Current/Pool of Reflection/Stirring Lights, E = Grim Visage/Gaze of the Abyss/Crushing Maw.
audit.corrected: Names fixed everywhere edited; W-shield interaction folded into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: Q 10s, W 18s, E 12s, R 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse gives you an answer, but level 6 still leans Hwei because landing it requires you to first tag him through his poke and disengage. He can pool away with EE (Stirring Sands) or QE before your Snare-into-ult connects. Bank the ult as an anti-dive and punish only when he misplays; the raw lane stays his until you finish an item.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse gives you an answer, but level 6 still leans Hwei because landing it requires you to first tag him through his poke and disengage. He can slip away with WQ (Fleeting Current) speed or a WW pool before your Snare-into-ult connects. Bank the ult as an anti-dive and punish only when he misplays; the raw lane stays his until you finish an item.

edits.before: You out-scale his safety: Rebuttal negates one big spell in a combo and Golden Eclipse resets fights by executing his carries, so teamfights favor you if you dodge his EQ (Fleeting Current) knock-up.
edits.after: You out-scale his safety: Rebuttal negates one big spell in a combo and Golden Eclipse resets fights by executing his carries, so teamfights favor you if you dodge his EW (Gaze of the Abyss) root.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are Hwei's strongest stretch and where most of your deficit lives; his layered Q combos zone you off the wave and he can all-in with EE reposition plus QQ execute if you fall low. Never blow Rebuttal proactively here since he baits it constantly. Freeze or last-hit safely, ping for a gank on his pushed-in waves, and just survive to your 6 spike.
